result.title: pi-Net: Empirical Latent Representations for Differentiable Physics Heads in Data-Scarce Systems
result.summary: Developing reliable predictive models for multi-physics systems often forces a compromise between computationally demanding physical simulators and data-hungry, opaque machine learning (ML) algorithms. While incorporating dimensional analysis into directed computation graphs offers a structurally sound alternative to explicitly solving partial differential equations (PDEs), such formulations typically yield underdetermined systems that act as imperfect simulators. We introduce pi-Net, a physics-informed latent variable model that resolves these imperfect simulators. The hybrid pi-Net architecture consists of an encoder that maps inputs into physically normalized latent space, which are then decoded into final predictions by a differentiable physics head. Evaluated on a real-world, data-scarce Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) case study, the framework achieves an R2 of 0.864 with only 60 experimental samples. The results demonstrate that pi-Net significantly outperforms purely data-driven baselines in data-scarce regimes while providing causal, process-level explainability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 pi-Net，一个物理信息潜变量模型：编码器将输入映射到物理归一化的 latent 空间，再由可微物理头部解码出预测，用以补全量纲分析计算图产生的欠定系统；在数据稀缺的 GMAW 焊接案例上仅用 60 个样本达到 R²=0.864。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构化归一化 latent 空间 + 可微解码头」的做法可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态的表示约束、状态抽象与可解释性有潜在概念联系，可供核查，但领域较远、不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
